**1. `lsp status` — how to actually see it**
Run it from the session, not from my side: in omp, invoke the LSP tool with `action=status` (the separate `lsp` tool, not a shell command). Headless equivalent:
```
omp -p --cwd C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\extensions\scholar "Call the lsp tool with action=status and print the result verbatim."
```
What it will report is per-server *resolution at startup*: your four dirs are on the **user** PATH, so they resolve only if this omp process inherited that PATH. This shell's own PATH is not the same thing as the process's, which is exactly why a stale launch shows them missing.

**2. Pin them by absolute path (only for the ones that don't resolve)**
Target file: `~/.omp/agent/lsp.json` → `C:\Users\basam\.omp\agent\lsp.json`. Content, using your inventory verbatim:

    "typescript-language-server": { "command": ["C:\\Users\\basam\\.bun\\bin\\typescript-language-server.exe", "--stdio"] },
    "pyright":   { "command": ["C:\\Users\\basam\\.bun\\bin\\pyright-langserver.exe", "--stdio"] },

`unverified — confirm first`: the exact top-level key/shape (`servers` map keyed by the built-in key, `command` as an argv array). I have not opened `omp://lsp-config.md` in this session; read it before writing, and drop any entry whose key it spells differently. Pinning `command` only — no `fileTypes`/`rootMarkers` — is right, since inheriting the built-ins is what you want.

Two notes: `tsc.exe` (`typescript-native`) is a checker, not a server — leave it built-in. And config is read at startup; after writing, `lsp reload *` re-reads it without restarting omp.

**3. The temp-dir root problem (this is your real blocker)**
This session is rooted at `C:\Users\basam\AppData\Local\Temp` — a **marker-less** directory: no `package.json`/`tsconfig.json` (TS/JS), no `pyproject.toml`/`setup.py`/`requirements.txt` (Python), no `compile_commands.json`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`.clangd` (C/C++), no `Cargo.toml` (Rust). With no root marker, servers either don't start or attach with no project, so "Python, TS/JS, C/C++, Rust working" is impossible from here regardless of PATH. Relaunch against a real root:
```
omp --cwd C:\Users\basam\.pi\agent\extensions\scholar        :: TS/JS (package.json present)
omp --cwd <dir with pyproject.toml>                          :: Python
omp --cwd <Rust crate dir>                                   :: rust-analyzer
omp --cwd <dir with compile_commands.json> --add-dir <second language root>
```
One session attaches servers for the languages whose markers exist under its roots; use `--add-dir` (repeatable) if you want TS + Python in one session.

**4. One-line verification after relaunch**
```
omp -p --cwd <project root> "lsp action=status" ; and in PowerShell: 'typescript-language-server','pyright-langserver','clangd','rust-analyzer' | % { (& $_ --version 2>$null | Select-Object -First 1) }
```
The second half proves the binaries run at all (PATH/exec independent of LSP handshakes); the first proves omp attached them to a root.
